spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The short-γ calculation works by splicing two applications of the polynomial convolution lemma so that the piecewise mollifier Q is represented on both sides of its breakpoint. After this compression, a contour integral that appears to have poles at ±τ actually has only the τ residue: reciprocal-zeta factors vanish to second order at −τ. An Euler-product/Perron estimate for the remaining square-free γ-sum then produces the factor 1−M^{-2τ(1−b)} with a controlled error.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For γ≤M^{1−b}, Lemma 6.1 is applied with R=P at scale M and with R(x)=1−P(b+x(1−b)) at scale M^{1−b}; their sum evaluates the Q-weighted a-sum, and the analogous b-sum follows with δ1 replaced by δ2. Substitution into the w-contour leaves one simple pole at w=τ because the reciprocal-zeta product kills the apparent w=−τ pole. Lemma 6.2 factors the square-free γ coefficients through ζ(s)F_w(s), uses Perron and contour shifting to obtain ζ(1+2τ)(1−x^{-2τ}), and yields (6.9), proportional to 1−M^{-2τ(1−b)} plus the stated shift-dependent error.
directed.conceptual_reading: The decisive move is to align the coefficient representation with the mollifier breakpoint before taking residues. This turns a nested convolution into a normalized multiplicative partial sum, while analytic zeros select which formal contour pole genuinely contributes. The computation separates local singular structure in w from global accumulation over γ.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are the two polynomial presentations of Q, the local factors G_w and H_w/h_w, the contour integrand in w, and the Dirichlet series ∑f_w(γ)γ^{-s}=ζ(s)F_w(s). The last representation exposes the ζ pole whose truncated mass is 1−x^{-2τ}; partial summation also bridges that estimate to smooth γ-weights.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The conclusion is confined to γ≤M^{1−b}, the prescribed contour and small-shift regime, and the chosen piecewise polynomial mollifier. The pole cancellation depends on exact reciprocal-zeta factors and does not follow merely from seeing formal denominators at ±τ. Lemma 6.2 supplies an asymptotic, not an exact finite identity, and this unit does not address the complementary long-γ range.
directed.uncertainty: The extraction is formula-sensitive: subscripts, products over signs, pole orders, and powers should be checked against the scan before exact reuse. The prose clearly supports the mechanism and (6.9), but some displayed formulas are visually compressed or potentially OCR-corrupted.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Above the mollifier breakpoint, the convolution residue no longer collapses to a constant: its Taylor coefficients expose Q, Q′, and Q′′. Lemma 6.2 converts the resulting γ-sum into a weighted integral N(w); the outer contour reduces this to N(τ) and N(−τ), and integration by parts uses the taper endpoint conditions to remove boundary clutter. Thus the detailed coefficient design survives only through a compact derivative functional of Q.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For M^{1−b}≤γ≤M, Lemma 6.1 expresses each Q-weighted inner sum as a residue at s=0 plus a decaying error. Expanding G_w(1+s,γ;u,v) divided by two zeta factors gives terms multiplying Q, Q′/log M, and Q′′/log²M; multiplying the δ1 and δ2 versions and applying Lemma 6.2 changes the γ-sum into the integral N(w) in (6.10). The w-contour is then evaluated through N(τ)−(8X/π)^{-2τ}N(−τ). Integration by parts with Q(0)=Q′(0)=0, Q(b)=1, and Q′(b)=0 yields the long-range term, which combines with (6.9) to give the M1 contribution (6.13).
directed.conceptual_reading: A local residue expansion translates arithmetic convolution into differential data of the taper. The subsequent summation and contour steps compress a high-dimensional coefficient calculation into two evaluations of one functional, N(±τ). Endpoint constraints are mathematically active: they determine which boundary terms remain, rather than serving as cosmetic smoothness assumptions.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The Taylor series at s=0 bridges reciprocal-zeta behavior to the differential operator acting on Q. Lemma 6.2 and a change of variables bridge the discrete square-free γ-range to an integral over x∈[0,b] weighted by M^{-2τ(1−x)}. N(w) packages that integral for the outer contour, while integration by parts exposes the endpoint data and the final square involving Q′ and Q′′/(2δ1 log M).
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is a calculation for one constrained polynomial taper and the long range M^{1−b}≤γ≤M; it does not establish optimality of Q or a general variational principle. The error estimates depend on the stated choices of M, contour C, and shift sizes. The reduction also relies on Lemma 6.2 and on exact endpoint identities; without them, extra boundary terms or uncontrolled remainders would remain.
directed.uncertainty: Representation dependence is very high. The extracted Taylor-coefficient sentence appears to label the coefficient of the quadratic contribution as a3 where the subsequent Q′′ term suggests a possible formula or OCR ambiguity, and one displayed G_w factor appears with an unexpected argument γ. Exact coefficients, denominators, and signs require scan verification, although the Q/Q′/Q′′ mechanism and N(±τ) reduction are explicit.
